jobs.title: Director, Finance (CSM)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

Type:
FullTime

Location:
Bolton, ON

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

Husky TechnologiesTM is committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If contacted in relation to a job opportunity or testing, you should advise the member of the Talent Acquisition team in a timely fashion of any disabilities that requires accommodation measures in order to enable you to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner.

Information received relating to accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.

No agency or telephone inquiries please.

jobs.title: Director, Financial & Business Analytics
jobs.description:
Date Posted: 11/02/2026

Req ID:50757

Faculty/Division: Faculty of Arts & Science

Department: Faculty Budget, Planning and Finance

Campus: St. George (Downtown Toronto)

Existing Vacancy: Yes

Description

About Us

The Faculty of Arts & Science is the heart of Canada’s leading university and one of the most comprehensive and diverse academic divisions in the world. The strength of Arts & Science derives from our combined teaching and research excellence in the humanities, sciences and social sciences across 29 departments, seven colleges and 46 interdisciplinary centres, institutes and programs. We can only realize our mission with the dedication and excellence of engaged staff and faculty. The diversity of opportunities and perspectives within the Faculty reflect the local and global landscape and the need for curiosity, innovative thinking and collaboration. At Arts & Science, we take pride in our legacy of innovation and discovery that has changed the way we think about the world.

Position Summary

The Director, Financial and Business Analytics works independently under the general direction of the Executive Director, Budget, Planning and Finance to develop and implement financial and accounting procedures, develop budget models, develop financial control procedures and ensure compliance with financial and accounting policies. The incumbent manages and produces complex data analysis relating to administrative matters across the Faculty of Arts & Science and provides related advanced financial/financial management recommendations and advice. In collaboration with the Manager, Faculty Budget & Finance the incumbent develops and implements annual budget and financial processes.

The incumbent reviews existing financial/administrative models, analyzes new programs and initiatives, calculates costs, prepares and audits financial models for completeness and viability, prepares and analyzes financial statements and reports using in depth knowledge of the Faculty and University planning environment. The incumbent plays an active role in the development and implementation of the Faculty of Arts & Science strategic short and long range budget plans and models. The incumbent performs operational/departmental audits and makes financial and business recommendations based on findings, including making recommendations on organizational restructuring, enabling data-driven leadership of organizational change within units of the Faculty.

The incumbent directly manages the Faculty’s business processes for the Dean’s Office portfolios, including the management of the Business Officer, and business support staff. This role is responsible for establishing best practice for business processes in the decanal portfolios and the broader Faculty business community.

Essential Qualifications

Education

University degree and completion of a recognized professional accounting program (CMA, CGA, or CA), or equivalent combination of education and experience

Experience

Minimum 8 years of related budgeting, accounting and financial analysis experience in a higher education environment, a large public sector setting or a large complex environment. Significant experience with university based administrative management systems (FIS, HRIS, and RIS) and with University budgeting/financial policies and procedures. Experience supervising staff in a unionized environment.

Skills

Advanced personal computer skills, particularly Excel and Access.
Advanced knowledge of the University’s Administrative management Systems (FIS, HRIS and RIS).
Proven ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, to a large and diverse community of stakeholders.
Effective and creative problem solver, with good judgement.
Demonstrated ability to plan and execute complex projects and manage conflicting priorities while working toward tight deadlines.
Able to assess information and make decisions and recommendations regarding matters confidential to labour relations.
Must have advanced knowledge of Excel, Access, ROSI, Word, AMS systems (FIS & HRIS).
Must have an excellent understanding of complex and varied computerized databases, and knowledge of the relevant and capabilities of various methods of retrieving data.

Other

Highly detail oriented and accurate with exceptional analytical skills.
Commitment to providing a high level of service to a large group of stakeholders.
Ability to take the initiative and respond to change.
Able to respect matters of a sensitive nature and maintain confidentiality.
Able to assess information and make decisions and recommendations regarding matters confidential to labour relations.
Ability to lead and assemble working groups and committees to discuss and assess projects that require input from many stakeholders and provide leadership to guide and oversee their efforts.
Proven analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
Must be able to translate statistical and analytical results into easily understood terms.
Demonstrated commitment to equity and diversity.
An excellent understanding of the objectives of the Faculty and an ability to effectively achieve the priorities of the Faculty.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO

Compensation: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary

Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, and our consumer product launches in January. Both run on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up to audit. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast and controls across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
Investor reporting: the financial model and board and investor updates
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and the numbers hold up to any scrutiny.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Business Transformation, Trust Co.
jobs.description:
BMO Trust Company is a leading provider of trust, estate, fiduciary, and wealth administration services, supporting high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families, and business owners across Canada. As part of BMO Private Wealth, BMO Trust works closely with Wealth Planning, Investment Management, Private Banking, and Trust & Estate professionals to deliver integrated solutions that help clients preserve, grow, and transfer wealth across generations.

The Senior Director, Business Transformation, Trust Co .,
leads the Trust Company's strategic growth, innovation, and transformation agenda. Responsible for identifying and executing initiatives that enhance client experience, drive business growth, and ensure the Trust Company remains aligned with evolving client needs, market opportunities, and Private Wealth priorities.

Fosters a culture aligned to BMO purpose, values and strategy and role models BMO values and behaviors in all that they do.
Ensures alignment between values and behavior that fosters diversity and inclusion.
Regularly connects work to BMO’s purpose, sets inspirational goals, defines clear expected outcomes, and ensures clear accountability for follow through.
Builds interdependent teams that collaborate across functional and operating groups to create the highest value for all stakeholders.
Attracts, retains, and enables the career development of top talent.
Improves team performance, recognizes and rewards performance, coaches employees, supports their development, and manages poor performance.
Monitors performance results at the national, market and sales-Trust professional level..
Identifies opportunities to grow business
Acts as a trusted advisor to senior leaders for making business decisions and implementing strategic initiatives.
Develops an expert understanding of business/group challenges.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Recommends business priorities, advises on resource requirements and develops roadmap for strategic execution.
Manages resources and leads the execution of strategic initiatives to deliver on business, technology and financial goals.
Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
Coordinates the management of databases; ensures alignment and integration of data in adherence with data governance standards.
Designs and produces regular and ad-hoc reports, financial reports and dashboards.
Leads change management programs of varying scope and type, including readiness assessments, planning, stakeholder management, execution, evaluation and sustainment of initiatives.
Leads the development and execution of the BMO Trust Company (internal and external) communications strategy, creating clear, impactful messaging that supports business objectives, strengthens employee and stakeholder engagement, and positively influences behaviors.
Leads / participates in the management of governance meetings including Board reporting and maintenance of governing body mandates, oversight and approval guidelines.
Leads/participates in the design, implementation and management of core business/group processes and technology investments
Oversees the provision of content and marketing materials for new business proposals e.g. special fee arrangements, technical information materials.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a senior specialist resource across BMO.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to multiple, interdependent, complex problems.
Fosters strong internal and external networks and works with and across multiple teams to achieve business objectives.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite while making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy. protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

9+ years of relevant experience in related field is required.
Professional Certifications and/or Advanced Degrees preferred: TEP.
Completion of the CFA, MBA, CA or LLB is an asset
Expert knowledge and technical proficiency related to private wealth management strategies, issues and trends
Broad and diverse background in financial service industry and expert knowledge of the banking services for the high net worth (HNW) markets
Expert knowledge of all applicable compliance and industry regulations.
Seasoned expert with extensive industry knowledge.
Technical leader viewed as a thought leader for innovation.
Verbal & written communication skills - Expert.
Analytical and problem solving skills - Expert.
Influence skills - Expert.
Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration - Expert.
Able to manage ambiguity.
Data driven decision making - Expert.

Salary:

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. To view more details of our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.bmo.com/global/en/Total-Rewards

About Us

At BMO we are driven by a shared Purpose: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life. It calls on us to create lasting, positive change for our customers, our communities and our people. By working together, innovating and pushing boundaries, we transform lives and businesses, and power economic growth around the world.

As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. We’ll support you with the tools and resources you need to reach new milestones, as you help our customers reach theirs. From in-depth training and coaching, to manager support and network-building opportunities, we’ll help you gain valuable experience, and broaden your skillset.

To find out more visit us at https://jobs.bmo.com/ca/en

BMO is committed to an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace. By learning from each other’s differences, we gain strength through our people and our perspectives. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. To request accommodation, please contact your recruiter.

Note to Recruiters: BMO does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to BMO, directly or indirectly, will be considered BMO property. BMO will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. A recruiting agency must first have a valid, written and fully executed agency agreement contract for service to submit resumes.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, and our consumer product launches in January. Both run on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up to audit. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast and controls across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

A seat at the leadership table

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and the numbers hold up to any scrutiny.

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
